texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of injury sustained by him in Motor Vehicle Accident. 2. The brief facts of the case of petitioner is as under: That on 23-05-2023 at about 5-40 p.m she was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/LE-5982 on the left side of 50 feet road, Avalahalli, Bangalore, when she reached near Nayara Petrol bunk, at that time, driver of Ambulance bearing Reg.No.KA-42/G-1041 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to her motor cycle and caused the accident. As a result of which she sustained grievous injuries. Immediately she was shifted to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bangalore wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3565/2023 Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, treatment, transportation, nourishment and other incidental charges. 3. It is contended that, prior to accident she was hale and healthy and she was a Tailor by profession and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries she could not able to do her day to day activities as earlier and suffering pain, mental shock and agony and also put to financial hardship. The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle and in this regard the Byatarayanapura Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of offending vehicle in Cr.No.191/2023 for the offences punishable u/sec.279 and 337 of IPC. The respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the Insurer of offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest and costs. 4. In response to issuance of notice, respondent no.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence he was placed exparte. On the other hand the respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed its written statement. 5. The respondent No.2 in its written statement contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case. While admitting about insurer (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3565/2023 of Ambulance bearing Reg.No.KA-42/G-1041 restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further this respondent denied the entire case of the petitioner. Further contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner herself, hence the petition is bad of non joinder of necessary parties. Further denied the age, income and avocation of petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and expenses Lavanya. The petitioner in order to prove the case, Petitioner herself got examined as PW.1 and also examined MRO of Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, as PW.2 and also examined Dr.Ramesh, working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore as PW.3. They got marked documents as Ex.P1 to 21. 8.
